thesis: The world's largest physically backed gold ETF: $141.0B AUM, ~34.0M oz (~1,059 t) of bullion, 0.40% expense ratio, NAV $379.97 against LBMA PM gold of $4,144.55/oz. The structural bid is the strongest of the cycle — record 289t of central bank net purchases in Q2 2026 and global gold-ETF holdings above 4,250t for the first time ever — but the cyclical driver has flipped: the Fed hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16 to 3.75-4.00%, the first increase since 2023, with better-than-even odds of another in October and the 30-year Treasury yield at a 22-year high. Gold is ~26% below its late-January 2026 record and GLD trades below a declining 50-day and 200-day average. Hold core allocations, stage new money, and prefer GLDM (0.10%) or IAUM (0.09%) for pure buy-and-hold given GLD's ~$564M annual fee drag.

base_case.assumptions: Fed funds peak near 4.25% then plateau through 2027; official-sector demand persists at 200t+ per quarter; Asian investment demand offsets record-weak jewellery volumes. Implies gold of ~$4,600-5,000/oz at the current ~0.0917 oz/share ratio, consistent with ICICI Bank's $4,600-5,000/oz H1 2027 range and UBS's reiterated $5,000/oz by H1 2027. Roughly +11% to +22% from $377.91.

key_risks: Fed actively hiking — 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, first increase since 2023, with one more signalled for 2026
Rising real yields; 30-year Treasury at 5.53%, highest since 2004, against a zero-yield asset
Dollar strength dominating price action; short-run correlations near -0.98
Negative price structure — ~26% below the late-January 2026 record, below declining 50-day ($395.62) and 200-day ($416.39) averages
0.40% expense ratio versus 0.09-0.25% for identical wrappers (GLDM, IAU, IAUM) — ~$564M/yr drag and persistent share rotation out of GLD ($603M redeemed in the week to 2026-09-12)
Zero income while cash yields near 4%, making opportunity cost material
Price-elastic demand destruction — Q2 jewellery demand of 278t was one of the weakest on record
Structural: shares are a claim on a trust, not allocated metal; no 1940 Act or Commodity Exchange Act protections; custody concentrated at HSBC and JPMorgan
Forced-liquidation reflexivity — GLD's liquidity makes it a first source of funds in a broad deleveraging, selling bullion into a falling market
